narrative_purpose: Shows the second killer at the deepest level: hydrogen sulfide jams the final enzyme that hands electrons to oxygen, so the cell suffocates while bathed in oxygen.
subject: A painterly close view of a mitochondrion's folded inner membrane. Along it, a glowing relay of electron carriers normally hands a bright spark down a chain toward oxygen - but at the final enzyme the chain is stalled and dark, choked by small pale sulfur-yellow molecules locked onto its iron heart. Plenty of cool oxygen motes drift nearby, unusable, just past the jammed door.
scene: An intimate cellular micro-scene; the membrane's curves filling the frame, the once-bright relay dimming toward the blocked terminal station.
camera: Extreme close micro view, shallow depth, following the membrane's fold across the frame to the jammed final enzyme.
light: The working part of the chain glows cyan-teal and alive; the light fails and goes cold-dark at the blocked enzyme where the pale sulfur molecules cluster.
palette: Cyan-teal living glow fading to cold indigo-dark at the jam, pale sickly sulfur-yellow on the blocking molecules, drifting cool oxygen motes.
style: Painterly speculative-biology micro-plate, hand-painted, organic, NOT a clinical schematic and NOT a 3D render.
detail_level: Crisp on the final enzyme and the pale sulfur molecules locking it; the rest of the chain softening into glow.
composition: The electron relay sweeping in from one side along the membrane, light dying toward the jammed terminal enzyme off-centre; unusable oxygen motes hovering past it.
consistency_notes: Pale sulfur-yellow is the chapter's consistent visual for hydrogen sulfide; cyan-teal is living energy. Reads as a painted micro-scene, not a biochemistry textbook figure.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no labels, no arrows, no chemical formulae, no schematic chrome, no photographic or 3D-render look, no lens flares
